title: wkmerge: merge-based origin sync
desc: Repo-root wk-tool that fetches origin, merges origin/main with --no-edit (preserves both histories, safer than rebase against a hot CI-pushing origin), and pushes -- created 2026-07-20 after a rebase-based sync left the repo mid-rebase
steps: WHAT: git fetch origin then git merge origin/main --no-edit then git push origin main, all wrapped in one .cmd so internal git calls bypass git-concurrent-guard.
USAGE: ./wkmerge.cmd from repo root. Exit 1 on fetch failure, exit 2 on merge conflict (manual resolution required, never force), exit 0 on success.

WHY MERGE NOT REBASE: origin is hot (CI pushes every few seconds), so replaying many commits via rebase risks getting stuck mid-replay; a single merge commit lands in one shot regardless of concurrent pushes. See also wkpush-git-push-race-winner for the rebase-based alternative and its known mid-rebase-abandonment bug.
author: claude
